chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Umar ibn Aasim, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

When Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him) reached the Stone before reaching the water spout, he would raise his head, then say: 'O Allah, enter me into Paradise by Your Mercy,' and while looking at the water spout, he would say: 'And save me by Your Mercy from the Fire, and grant me well-being from illness, and expand for me from the permissible sustenance, and turn away from me the evil of the wicked of the Jinn and humans, and the evil of the wicked of the Arabs and non-Arabs.'

key_terms.الْمِيزَاب: The water spout of the Kaaba

ai.seo_question: What is the specific supplication recited by the Imams when reaching the Mizab during Hajj or Umrah?
ai.summary: This narration from al-Kafi highlights the specific devotional practice of Imam Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS), who, upon reaching the Mizab (water spout) of the Kaaba, raised his gaze to seek divine mercy comprehensively. His supplication integrates entry into Paradise, protection from Hellfire, physical health, and halal sustenance, while specifically invoking deliverance from the mischief of both Jinn and humans, as well as Arabs and non-Arabs. This reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on the Kaaba not merely as a structural landmark but as a focal point for holistic spiritual and worldly supplication.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Umar Bin Aasim, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:

‘It was so that whenever Ali<sup>asws</sup> Bin Al-Husayn<sup>asws</sup> reached the (Black) Stone before reaching the water spout, raised his<sup>asws</sup> head, then he<sup>asws</sup> was saying: ‘Enter me<sup>asws</sup> into the Paradise by Your<sup>azwj</sup> Mercy’, and he<sup>asws</sup> was looking at the water spout: ‘And Save me<sup>asws</sup>, by Your<sup>azwj</sup> Mercy, from the Fire, and Make me well from the illness, and Expand upon me<sup>asws</sup> from the Permissible sustenance, and Turn away from me<sup>asws</sup> the evil of the wicked Jinns and the humans, and evil of the wicked Arabs and non-Arabs’.
en.sarwar: 5. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from ibn abu ‘Umayr from ‘Umar ibn ‘Asem who has said the following: “Abu `Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said that when Ali ibn al-Husayn, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, would go near the Black Stone, before reaching al-Mizab, raise his head and say, £ 0 Allah, admit me in paradise through Your mercy and kindness/ and look at al-Mizab. Then he would say, ‘O Allah, grant me protection through Your mercy against hellfire, grant me good health against illnesses, increase my sustenance from Your lawful provisions, and keep away from me the wickedness of sinful Satan in the form of Jinn, man, Arab and non- Arab people/”
